steps: This video shows why one slow call can stall a whole service, and how async fixes it. Traffic spikes, and three tickets hit TicketFlow at once: a double charge, a crash, and a dark mode request.
TicketFlow runs Flask with a synchronous client. It sends ticket one to Claude and then blocks the event loop while it waits, so nothing else can move.
Reply one finally returns, but tickets two and three have been waiting the whole time, and those requests start to time out.
So you switch the client to Async Anthropic. Now every call to messages create is awaitable, which means the service can wait on many calls without blocking.
With asyncio gather, TicketFlow fires all three calls at once. Claude has three requests in flight together, and the event loop never blocks.
Peak traffic triggers a four twenty nine rate limit. The S D K retries automatically with backoff, here up to three retries with a thirty second timeout, so you write no manual retry loop.

All three results land together: billing, technical and feature request, with the latency of one call, not three. The takeaway: concurrent async calls keep a service responsive. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
